articles.title: Fernando Alonso: What's the latest on Aston Martin driver's future as he weighs up retirement or new contract to stay in F1 in 2027?
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso's future became a major talking point in Madrid after FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said he wants to help engine manufacturer Honda; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Alonso has been frustrated with Formula 1's 2026 regulations and the performance of his Aston Martin-Honda car, having scored points just twice this season.

The 45-year-old, whose current contract at Aston Martin expires at the end of this season, suggested how he feels about the power unit tweaks for next year, which will see the electric output reduced from its current near 50 per cent to 42 per cent, will dictate his decision.

"It's a matter of understanding what the rules from next year will have an impact or not on the racing and on the driving side of things," said Alonso last Thursday at the Spanish Grand Prix.

"The current cars, as I said many times, are not the best cars to drive and to enjoy. But next year there is a step in the right direction, hopefully.

"At the same time, I need to think what is the best programme for next year and sit with the team. Behind the wheel or in another role, where I will be helping the most, that will be the most important thing to decide together."

Are FIA set to help Honda to keep Alonso in F1?

A day after Alonso's comments, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem appeared to reveal he wants to accelerate Honda's engine development so they can catch up.

"There is no way we can allow Fernando to leave - Alonso, a great champion - just because of the circumstances. That's not the way to leave the stage," said Ben Sulayem.

"He has to be successful and then he leaves whenever he wants, not because he was forced to leave because of the performance.

"I share the issues. The car is not performing. I met with Lawrence [Stroll] on Thursday and I'm going to do the changes and will talk to him to make him, try to make him, change his mind. It's not acceptable."

The comments could be seen as a personal intervention by Ben Sulayem but Sky Sports F1 understands the FIA president wants to work with the Power Unit Advisory Committee, which features all five engine manufactures, to work together to help Honda.

One option could be changing the ADUO (Additional Development Upgrades Opportunities) rules to not only be about the ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) power.

Honda have already used one of two engine upgrade opportunities this year, have at least another two for 2027 and were given an extra £14m of development budget.

Ben Sulayem added: "I will be speaking to him. I said to him, I saw him very sad, and I said, 'Fernando, I understand, it's not acceptable that you are coming to your own country and now after two times a world champion and you are at the last'.

"We did something earlier, in May, legally for the team towards the engine to go and improve, and then I said to him, 'I am not going to tell you what we are going to do. Please tell me what you want because you are the driver and come and tell me what do you want us to do to improve these results.'

"Suddenly you see everything change, then I get a call and I had a meeting [with Stroll]. We are here to support."

Red Bull were deemed to have the best engine earlier this year by the FIA, although most people in the paddock feel Mercedes are the benchmark engine manufacturer.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies are open to changes in order for Honda can catch up.

"The ADUO in that case was designed as a catch-up mechanism and that formula was unlocked for Honda, and they need more," said Wolff.

"And the conversation that the president had with Alonso is fair enough. We want to have all of these top constructors in the sport. We want them to be competitive and successful.

"And regulations are regulations to be for the best of the sport and sometimes maybe they need an adjustment, so fair enough conversation."

Mekies added: "As much as we cannot agree all the time, as a sport we try to keep a fairly open look at the regulations.

"You may recall that actually there was a first change in the ADUO regulations done earlier this year precisely in order to help those who were much behind, compared to what was initially voted. All the teams voted that, we voted in favour of that for the benefit of the sport.

"As I said, we cannot agree on everything but certainly as stakeholders of the sport if there is a situation that needs to be fixed or needs to be supported, we normally find solutions. And I'm sure that we will at some stage sit down and discuss the future of the ADUO regulations. The shortfalls, we know some of them, and I'm sure there is a few of those to address later on."

So is Alonso going to stay or retire from F1?

It is hard to judge whether Alonso's initial comments were sparked by a push to get rule changes which will aid Aston Martin and Honda, or he's genuinely unhappy with the current F1 cars.

Perhaps it is a combination of both and it should not be forgotten Alonso made his F1 debut in 2001 - an era with roaring normally aspirated V10 engines - a contrast to now.

There will certainly be an element of Aston Martin not being competitive too which is part of Alonso's thinking and that brings us to how long does the Spaniard want to race in F1 for, if he can't compete at the front?

Alonso will be 46 years old next summer and the last driver to race in F1 at that age was Graham Hill in 1975. The Spaniard became a father earlier this year and hinted he still has other motorsport ambitions after admitting a return to the World Endurance Championship and the Le Mans 24 Hours is an option.

Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack said at the weekend in Madrid: "We were always clear the team wants to continue. We have made it clear all through, but we need to respect what Fernando's thoughts are.

"We need to respect the time he wants to take. And, as I said before, we're confident we can reach a good solution for everybody. And now it's about waiting. He needs to make up his mind and then we move on."

Most of the 2027 F1 grid is locked in after Max Verstappen signed a new Red Bull contract and Williams duo Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon committed to staying for next year.

Only the second Red Bull seat alongside Verstappen, Racing Bulls, Haas and Audi are yet to confirm their line-ups so Aston Martin won't have the option to sign a perceived top driver to replace Alonso, should he retire.

Krack said: "I will also not speak about any Plan B. We very much hope that Fernando will continue. He's very important for our team. He's very important for Formula 1. He's very important for the whole sport and motorsport in general.

"It would be a pity to not have him anymore. And because that would be so dramatic, I do not even want to talk about it or think about it."

articles.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Fairy Glen well fancied in John Musker Fillies' Stakes feature at Yarmouth
articles.summary: Simon & Ed Crisford's Fairy Glen drops back down to Listed level in the John Musker at Yarmouth on Wednesday; Ryan Moore in action at the Norfolk track; watch every race live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
3.41 Yarmouth - Fairy Glen, Seet & Rhapsody clash

The EBF Stallions John Musker Fillies' Stakes is the feature on an excellent midweek card at Yarmouth.

Simon & Ed Crisford-trained filly Fairy Glen tops the ratings with a mark of 112, and this Group Two winner could prove hard to beat in this lesser grade. She was only narrowly beaten when fifth in the Group One Prix Vicomtesse Vigier back in May and has obvious claims if fit enough on her return.

Rhapsody is a key player for William Haggas and Tom Marquand. A dual winner, she has filled the runner-up spot on her last two outings, and a similar effort would see her in the mix.

Seet is lightly-raced and should have more to offer, while Sky Safari has not been seen since finished third in the Group Three Hoppings Stakes at Newcastle and looks an each-way player on the switch to the turf.

4.12 Yarmouth - Unbeaten Enoch makes handicap debut

Ryan Moore has a 24 per cent strike-rate from over 100 rides at Yarmouth and heads to Norfolk to ride Enoch , who bids to remain unbeaten in a strong edition of the Goffs Two Million Series Handicap.

John & Thady Gosden's charge made it two from two when defying a penalty at Lingfield last month and, given his pedigree, he rates an exciting addition to handicap company.

Round The Table built on his debut to land a maiden and a novice before racing too keenly when beaten on handicap debut last time. He is given another chance with the tongue-tie removed.

Plenty have chances including the consistent El Matador , while Point Of Contact was beaten favourite at Salisbury and has a bit to prove.

3.06 Yarmouth - Liberty's Hall looks to go one better

Liberty's Hall hopes to build on an encouraging debut in the EBF Future Stayers Maiden Stakes.

James Owen's son of Nathaniel showed inexperience when chasing home Sonic Angel on his first start at Kempton last month and given natural progression he should hit the frame.

Nostalgic Warrior is a brother to the useful Star Performer and Divine Rhythm must be monitored in the betting on his debut for William Haggas.

Richard Hughes' Daddy Star is worth a mention, while Chapel Stream was only seventh on his debut and his trainer reaches for the cheekpieces.

articles.title: Senna Agius sube a MotoGP de la mano del KTM Tech3
articles.standfirst: El piloto Australiano subirá a la categoría reina gracias a la marca Austriaca, ocupando así el segundo asiento del equipo francés
articles.summary: El piloto Australiano subirá a la categoría reina gracias a la marca Austriaca, ocupando así el segundo asiento del equipo francés
articles.body: MotoGP confirma el ascenso de Senna Agius a la categoría reina. El australiano correrá con los colores naranjas de KTM y como compañero de Luca Marini. El cambio de reglamento para 2027 ha traído un cambio de asientos en la categoría reina. A principios de verano se anunciaba el fichaje de Álex Márquez y Fabio Di Giannantonio por el Red Bull KTM Factory Team, ocupando así los puestos de Pedro Acosta, quien será parte del Ducati Lenovo Team, y Brad Binder, recientemente anunciado en el Mundial de WorldSBK. Como pilotos satélites, se anunció en un primer momento el fichaje de Luca Marini, quien cedería su asiento a David Alonso o Diogo Moreira, aún por confirmar, en el Honda HRC Castrol como compañero de Fabio Quartararo, y ocuparía el puesto de Enea Bastianini, quien se va al SuperFile Track House MotoGP Team. Ahora ha llegado el turno de Senna Agius, quien actualmente está luchando contra su compañero de equipo, Manu González, por el mundial de Moto2. El piloto del Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP, acaba de ser anunciado como piloto oficial de MotoGP en el equipo del Red Bull KTM Tech3, ocupando así el puesto que deja Maverick Viñales. El Mundial de MotoGP ha dejado muy claro en numerosas ocasiones que quiere abrir las puertas a más nacionalidades, por lo que la marcha de Jack Miller al WorldSBK, dejaba un puesto libre como australiano a Senna Agius, quien ha demostrado además, merecer un asiento en MotoGP, al ser uno de los candidatos al título de Moto2. Por otra parte, se ha de tener en cuenta la entrada de un nuevo circuito australiano a partir de la próxima temporada, sustituyendo al mítico Philip Iland: el circuito de Adelaide, el cuál necesitará un buen representante. Con su futuro ya resuelto, el piloto australiano podrá seguir centrado en la lucha por el Mundial y ver si es capaz de subir el título con él a la máxima categoría del motociclismo. Además, con este fichaje se resuelve casi por completo la parrilla 2027 de MotoGP, a la espera, como previamente hemos mencionado, de ver quién estará en el equipo oficial y en el satélite de Honda: David Alonso o Diogo Moreira.

articles.title: F1 2027 calendar announced with Bahrain to host season-opener and increase in Sprint weekends in 24-race schedule
articles.summary: Bahrain to host 2027 Formula 1 season-opener as Portugal and Turkey return to the schedule from next year, plus an increase in Sprint weekends; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
For a fourth consecutive year, there are 24 rounds scheduled with Portugal's Portimao and Turkey's Istanbul Park returning to the calendar.

As expected, the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the schedule while the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya moves into a rotational deal with Spa-Francorchamps that will see the Spanish event held in even numbered years from 2028 and the Belgian Grand Prix held in odd numbered years from 2027.

F1 had delayed its calendar announcement for next year due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has created uncertainty over the end of the current season with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still currently scheduled to take place later this year.

Bahrain will host a four-day pre-season test on February 24-27 before holding the 2027 season-opener on March 12-14 and it will be a Sprint weekend, with the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix a week later.

Australia reverts to the third round of the season in early April and will also host a Sprint, as will the next race in Japan before China rounds off a triple-header.

Miami retains its slot in the first weekend of May before Sprint rounds in Canada and, for the first time, Monaco, with F1 highlighting fans are "set to enjoy two thrilling qualifying sessions" around the streets of Monte Carlo.

The returning Portuguese Grand Prix slots into mid-June and is followed by a Sprint weekend at the British Grand Prix on July 2-4, with Austria moving to after Silverstone.

Back-to-back weekends in Belgium and Hungary will take the F1 circus to the summer break.

A sprint round at Monza in early September will be the first event back after five weeks off, a week longer than usual, with the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid a week later.

Azerbaijan, Turkey and Singapore form part of a triple-header before the usual Americas triple-header in Austin, Mexico and Brazil, which is a Sprint weekend.

Las Vegas will host the only Saturday race of 2027, although it will be Sunday morning in the UK, then two Sprint weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi on December 10-12 conclude the season.

"The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said F1 president Stefano Domenicali.

"We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Turkey to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to 10 events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special.

"Formula 1 continues to go from strength-to-strength, attracting new audiences around the globe. Week after week, the world's greatest drivers will battle on some of the most challenging tracks in motorsport, supported by F1's outstanding teams, world-class manufacturers, and global partners. Together, they create a spectacle unlike anything else in sport. As we continue this remarkable journey of growth, I want to thank our fans around the world as their passion drives everything we do."

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added: "The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport.

"With 24 Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Turkey, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

articles.standfirst: Un nuevo 'Inside' (dentro) de Ducati releva los secretos de la remontada de Marc Márquez
articles.summary: Un nuevo 'Inside' (dentro) de Ducati releva los secretos de la remontada de Marc Márquez
articles.body: Terminado el Gran Premio de San Marino, Ducati ha vuelto a publicar los secretos de un fin de semana de Gran Premio en un nuevo episodio de 'Inside' (Dentro) de Ducati. El episodio comienza viéndose a 'Pecco' Bagnaia en un evento junto a Marco Bezzecchi y Franco Morbidelli, disfrutando de otro de sus deportes preferidos: el baloncesto. Mientras Marc Márquez se sorprendía al ver el cambio de look de Marco Rigamonti, el ingeniero de pista de Marc, al teñirse de rubio y con lo que Marc bromeó: "Como Vegeta (personaje de Dragon BallZ), que cuando se volvía amarillo iba rápido." A lo que Rigamonti respondió: "Ya sabes... mañana gel (en el pelo)." Además, ante la prensa el 9 veces Campeón del Mundo aclaró el porqué de la foto diciendo: "He posteado esa foto, porque he sentido que era el mejor momento para hacerlo." Marc Márquez ha tenido en todo momento el fin de semana bajo control y así lo ha sentido. Además, también se ha visto el cariño de los fans italianos, los cuales poco a poco empiezan a sentirle uno más de los suyos, al ser capaz de llevar a Ducati a lo más alto. El español confía en su moto y así lo ha dejado ver en el episodio al confirmárselo a Juan Miranda (futbolista), que se encontraba de visita: "Corre mucho. Incluso demasiado." En todo momento ha sabido qué neumático escoger, el medio, diciéndole a su equipo: "siempre hay que hacer caso al piloto." Además, desde el primero momento ha sabido su punto débil, el tercer sector, perdiendo en la salida de la curva 10, tal y como se lo explicaba a su equipo tras la sesión de clasificación, tras la cuál bromeaba con Marco Bezzecchi: "Cuando he visto 29 he dicho... adiós pole." La Sprint también estaba bajo control. A pesar de sus dudas con el neumático medio, Marc apostó por él reafirmando su decisión para el domingo. Sin embargo, el que tuvo un momento de duda fue 'Gigi' Dall'Igna, quien confesó haber sentido miedo al ver a Marc ralentizar durante unas vueltas en la Sprint. Ante esto, Marc le respondió: "porque he pensado que los otros se habían rendido y cuando he visto que no he dicho... venga va." Tal y como le pasó durante la carrera larga del domingo, cuando Marc confesó haberse relajado al ver que Bezzecchi se iba al suelo, lo que hizo que el ataque de Jorge Martín le pillara por sorpresa: "No se lo esperaba", decían desde el box del español. Mientras, la cruz de la moneda se la sigue llevando 'Pecco', quien afirma saber qué es lo que les diferencia de los demás y que tiene claro que no puede competir. Aún y así, el italiano al correr en casa estrenó casco; esta vez un homenaje a Manuel Poggiali, dos veces Campeón del Mundo de motociclismo y actualmente 'coach' de pilotos de Ducati. La efusividad que siempre muestra Davide al ver a sus pilotos cruzar primeros la línea de meta es un claro ejemplo de lo que le gusta a Ducati ganar. A pesar de las dudas que recaen sobre Ducati ante su clara desventaja este año contra la Aprilia, Tardozzi sigue apostando por sus pilotos y, al ver a Marc, no solo ganar la carrera y llevarse los 37 puntos del fin de semana, sino colocarse líder del mundial, el jefe de equipo estalló de alegría: "È rosso!!" (Es rojo), frase que se escuchó por primera vez el año pasado tras la Sprint en Mugello en reacción contra los pitos que los italianos lanzaban a su piloto español. Con este episodio se muestra el cariño y la gratitud que cada vez más italianos están teniendo con Marc Márquez, dejando de lado poco a poco lo sucedido en 2015 y aceptando que tal vez Marc puede escribir una gran historia con el equipo italiano.

articles.title: F1 2027 calendar: Monaco staging one of 10 Sprints and other talking points from race schedule reveal for next season
articles.summary: Assessing the increase in Sprint races for the 2027 Formula 1 season, including Monaco, plus other changes to the sport's racing schedule; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
But the schedule features a number of points of intrigue including an increase in Sprints, headlined by the addition of Monaco, the continued presence of the sport's usual Middle Eastern rounds, and the return of two popular tracks...

As reported in July , Formula 1 is increasing the number of Sprint weekends on the calendar for 2027.

The final number of Sprints has been confirmed as 10, four more than the six which have featured in each of the past four seasons.

The alternative format, which was first introduced in 2021 and features an additional qualifying session to set the grid for a short-form 100km race, has led to increase in global television audiences, which F1 says are 12 per cent higher than on non-Sprint weekends which feature three practice sessions.

The 10 venues for 2027 are split evenly between tracks that have staged Sprints previously - Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, Interlagos and Qatar's Lusail - and newcomers to the format in Sakhir, Albert Park, Suzuka, Monaco and Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina Circuit.

The current Sprint format, which features points for the top-eight finishers, is thought set to remain the same for 2027.

Why Monaco is staging a first-ever Sprint

Certainly, many of the early headlines and debate around the 2027 calendar has centred on the fact Monaco has unexpectedly been included as one the 10 Sprint venues.

Not only has the Principality never hosted a Sprint before, its main 78-lap Grand Prix is already not known for overtaking around its narrow, twisty wall-lined circuit with the race often proving processional in dry conditions.

It is regularly Qualifying - and the flat-out challenge of threading an F1 car between the barriers - that proves the most jaw-dropping aspect of the Monaco weekend. F1 has pointed out that the addition of the Sprint means there will now be two such grid-setting sessions in 2027

It can also be argued that having only one practice session, rather than the usual three, offers the chance for more unpredictability in the pecking order given drivers will only have one practice session to build rhythm and confidence, a crucial element of a successful Monaco weekend.

"Traditionally Sprints have been held at tracks where it is easy to overtake. Clearly that's not the case at Monaco," said Sky Sports' Craig Slater.

"But the big bonus here we'll have two red-hot qualifying sessions. That's what that track is all about and the drivers will have the ultimate test on two occasions that weekend."

For the first time next year, the season will both start and finish with a Sprint event.

Bahrain opens the season with the format on March 12-14 while Abu Dhabi will close it on December 10-12.

The season-opening Sprint will certainly present a different challenge for teams and drivers given they will have just one practice session that weekend to prepare for the campaign's first competitive session, Sprint Qualifying, on the Friday evening.

However, pre-season testing at the same Sakhir circuit (February 24-27) will run to four rather than three days - one more day than is usually the case outside of years featuring big rule changes - meaning they will at least be familiar with the track with the new 2027 cars.

Still, the season-opening Sprint represents a new challenge and could offer some early-season surprises in the pecking order for one, or both, grids if teams are not on top of their cars and set-ups.

The fact that the season will finish with back-to-back Sprint events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi inevitably raises the possibility of the world title being decided in a Saturday race should the fight go down to the final rounds.

There is already precedent for this from Qatar 2023 when Max Verstappen clinched his third world title in the Sprint.

Middle East races scheduled as F1 waits on final 2026 decisions

The sport's four Middle Eastern races all feature on the 2027 season, bookending the 24-race campaign.

That also remains the case for 2026's final two scheduled races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi with just over two months to go until the sport is due to head there.

The conflict in the Middle East has already seen this year's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix cancelled and the Bahrain Grand Prix moved to Malaysia on October 4, having originally been scheduled for April at its own Sakhir track a week before Jeddah.

F1's intention and planning remains for 2026's concluding two rounds to go ahead as scheduled. Although Stefano Domenicali had previously indicated that there was a mid-September timeframe on making a final decision on whether the events could take place, there is thought to be no hard deadline as such with officials able to wait for longer before making a final call.

Italy's Imola circuit is understood to be the contingency to close the current season in December should the Middle Eastern rounds not be able to take place.

The early-season 2027 dates in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia are not scheduled for another five months, giving F1 and the FIA plenty of time to continue monitoring the latest situation.

Formula 1's calendar first increased to a record 24 grands prix in 2024 and that number is again scheduled for next year.

Next year's calendar features no absolutely-new venues, but the sport will return to Portugal and Turkey for the first time since the popular European venues were called up to help out during the Covid-affected 2020 and 2021 seasons.

They replace the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, which starts a rotation with the Belgian GP and next returns in 2028, and Dutch Grand Prix, whose deal has ended.

Portugal's Portimao circuit takes over Barcelona's June slot, while Turkey returns at the start of October as part of a slightly rejigged run of races after F1's summer break, which will stretch to five weeks in 2027.

The season will finish on December 12, one week later than this year and the latest since 2020.
